title: Add admin bulk-delete, tag-filter, and JSON export to Flask blog
description: A Flask blog with post management needs three hard admin features: bulk delete, tag-based filter on public and API views, and a JSON export endpoint.

task_spec.prompt:
The Flask blog in src/app.py has public views (/, /posts/<id>), an admin page (/admin), and a JSON API (/api/posts, POST /api/posts). Add three hard features:

Feature 1 — Bulk delete: Add POST /admin/bulk-delete that accepts a JSON body {"ids": [1, 2, 3]}. Delete all posts with matching IDs. Return JSON {"deleted": N} where N is the count of actually deleted posts (IDs that did not exist are silently ignored). Return 400 if 'ids' key is missing or not a list.

Feature 2 — Tag filter: Update GET / (HTML) and GET /api/posts (JSON) to accept an optional ?tag=<name> query param. Filter to posts that include that tag (case-insensitive). When combined with the existing published-only logic on both views, the tag filter applies after the published filter.

Feature 3 — JSON export: Add GET /api/export that returns all posts (published AND drafts) as a JSON array. Accept an optional ?published=true|false param to filter: ?published=true returns only published, ?published=false returns only drafts, absent returns all. Add a Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=posts.json header so browsers treat it as a download.

Add tests in tests/test_blog.py covering: bulk delete removes correct posts, bulk delete with unknown IDs returns deleted=0 for those, tag filter on /api/posts, export all, export published only. All 6 original tests must still pass. Run uv run pytest tests/ -q to confirm.
required_artifacts: GET /api/export with ?published= param and Content-Disposition header
5 new tests covering all three features
success_criteria: Bulk delete handles partial hits gracefully
Tag filter case-insensitive and composes with published filter
Export returns all posts including drafts by default
followup_prompts: Good. Now handle edge cases: what does the UI show when data is empty, loading, or an error occurs? Add those states and tests.
Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to verify the complete implementation. Fix any failures and confirm all UI states work correctly.
